items.summary: Multi-agent active inference gives a natural account of belief sharing: agents hold local posteriors over a shared latent state, communicate those beliefs, and pool them into a colony-level consensus. The same mechanism is fragile when a member is miscalibrated, corrupted, or strategically wrong. Because the standard pool multiplies the reports together, a single confident-but-wrong broadcast that puts near-zero mass on the true state can pull the whole consensus off it, outweighing many honest members. The colony therefore needs a way to preserve the useful structure of belief sharing while limiting the influence of contaminated beliefs. This paper presents Active Fedference, a discrete-categorical framework that connects robust federated generalized variational inference with active inference belief sharing. The main bridge is structural: standard belief sharing appears as the non-robust corner of a broader generalized-Bayes family, while robust losses, conservative server fusion, and explicit aggregation diagnostics describe how the system moves away from that corner under declared contamination mechanisms. The result is not a replacement for belief sharing, but a containment result: ordinary belief sharing is recovered when robustness is turned off. Bounded-loss theory applies on the client axis, while the variational-server axis supplies an objective-backed redescending weight update. Following the manuscript's authoritative three-axis guarantee map, the paper keeps source-conditional client updates, a recovery-only heuristic server rule, and an objective-backed variational server rule as separate claim owners, with no robustness guarantee transferred between them. The study suite then exercises the framework as an end-to-end research system: recovery checks anchor the standard-Bayes limit, belief-sharing studies verify the communication baseline, contamination experiments test robust consensus, and extension studies probe moving agents, hierarchical latent structure, sensitivity to acuity and colony size, parameter recovery, and single-host socket-backed federation traces. All reported quantities are generated from deterministic analysis artifacts and injected into the manuscript by token, so the paper, figures, release package, and validation reports remain tied to the same execution record. The open-source repository is ActiveInferenceInstitute/Active_Fedference. This final-release manuscript uses assigned version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22149133; the bound deposited PDF and repository release are controlled by separate publication gates.
items.title: Robust Belief Sharing in Federated Active Inference: A Recovery-Tested Generalized-Variational Framework for Categorical Contamination-Aware Consensus

items.summary: This paper refines the finiteness conjecture for stability architectures and establishes the strongest currently provable results. A stability claim is treated as a profile specifying the object, state space, evolution, perturbation class, projection, failure region, time horizon, and obstructing gap or invariant. An architecture abstracts the structural core: the category of state spaces, the operator class, the gap functional, and the transport obstruction. The paper proves that stability cannot be classified from the trajectory map alone; the full profile matters. For linear systems, there are exactly three distinct architectures: dissipative, geometric or gradient, and Hamiltonian. For model-theoretic stability, the classification is finite and known: stability, NIP, simplicity, and rosiness. This logical classification is an analogy, not a direct translation to dynamics. For Hamiltonian systems, conditional finiteness identifies five candidate mechanisms: KAM persistence, Nekhoroshev confinement, Trojan resonance-gap suppression, symmetry constraint, and barrier obstruction. For statistical systems, four candidates appear: uniform, partial, and non-uniform hyperbolicity, plus rate conditions. In both cases, finiteness follows only if the lists are exhaustive, which remains conjectural. The paper also proves an intra-architecture transfer theorem, a qualified cross-architecture rigidity theorem, and a proposition on overlapping architectures. Transfer works within a shared architecture because estimates depend only on structural data. Rigidity blocks transfer between structurally distinct architectures unless additional structure exists. Overlap is possible, allowing multiple stability mechanisms and multiple failure routes. The general classification problem is undecidable, proved by reduction from the halting problem. Limitations include autonomous, finite-dimensional, smooth dynamics; time-dependent, infinite-dimensional, non-smooth, and nonlinear cases remain open. The consequences concern analog laboratories, engineering design by architecture selection, and a finite core of stability theory. The central message is that the finiteness conjecture is not vacuous: it holds where testable, while full generality awaits resolution of the exhaustiveness conjectures.
items.title: Stability Architectures: A Finite Classification of Provable Cases

items.summary: Hashing Is Not Retrieval is a prospectively frozen three-arm evaluation of context accumulation in small-model multi-agent code cartography. It compares three ways for an orchestrator to hand work to a worker: 1. FULL HISTORY — retransmit prior worker outputs. 2. OPAQUE REF — replace the previous output with an unretrievable SHA-256 digest. 3. RETRIEVED — resolve the digest through a tenant-scoped content-addressed store and inject the recovered bytes. All arms receive identical source-derived evidence. The apparatus measures the exact message content sent to workers and records token counts, model and provider identifiers, generation IDs, usage, cost, retries, and retrieval proofs. A five-task gate preceded a fixed 50-task controlled benchmark, followed by a separate state-required evaluation across 24 deterministic fixtures and a five-scale Medusa case study. Key result: in the controlled benchmark, RETRIEVED reduced paired peak context by 38.3% relative to FULL HISTORY. The state-required follow-up shows that opaque references fail when state must be recovered, while verified retrieval preserves substantially more structural information. This is bounded-context evidence for automatic orchestrator-resolved state passing inside a specific two-worker code-cartography harness — not a universal claim about autonomous memory, long-context capability, or reasoning quality. The release includes the corrected author-identified preprint, executable apparatus, frozen results, task fixtures, telemetry, and verification instructions. Version 1.0.2 supplies the curated, verifier-passing reproducibility archive. It supersedes the uncurated archive from version 1.0.1 and includes the exact pinned apparatus, state-required fixtures, frozen results, and archive verifier. Submission status: This preprint was submitted to the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Long Context Foundation Models (LCFM). LCFM is a non-archival workshop; this Zenodo record is a public preprint and does not indicate acceptance or publication. Workshop information: https://longcontextfm.github.io/ Research website: https://abdulmoizahmed.com/research Concept DOI (all versions): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22844754 License: CC BY 4.0.
items.title: Hashing Is Not Retrieval: A Three-Arm Study of Context Accumulation in Small-Model Code Cartography

items.summary: This paper offers a critical analysis of the European Union as a model of regional integration and examines its contribution to peace and to the effectiveness of the United Nations system. Set against the background of the failure of the League of Nations, the study argues that the post-1945 international order has endured largely because it is supported by strong regional institutions. Using the EU as the primary case study, the paper contends that by institutionalizing peace within Europe through economic interdependence, binding law, and supranational governance, the EU has created a zone of stability that reduces the burden on global governance structures. Furthermore, the paper analyzes how the EU functions as a support pillar for the United Nations under Chapter VIII of the UN Charter. Through financial contributions, peacekeeping partnerships, and coordinated diplomacy, the EU has reinforced multilateralism and provided capacity for conflict management and development. A comparative perspective is also drawn with other regional bodies such as ECOWAS to demonstrate a broader pattern of regional-global cooperation. The paper concludes that the longevity of the United Nations, compared to the League of Nations, can be partly explained by this two-level architecture of global and regional governance. While the EU’s support for the UN is substantial, it is also inconsistent, as internal EU divisions sometimes undermine collective action. Ultimately, the study shows that effective regional integration is a critical condition for sustaining peace and strengthening the United Nations system.
items.title: The European Union and Regional Integration: A Critical Analysis of Peacebuilding and Support for the United Nations System

items.summary: ElectromagneticFields v0.9.0 Diff since v0.8.0 Breaking Changes Everything here that requires a change to calling code, and what to do about it. The sections below give the reasoning; this is the checklist. @code , its seven per-preset variants, code and load_equilibrium are gone. Generated code is no longer injected into a module. Build a field by calling FieldFunctions(equ) , which returns a value: it can be constructed inside a function, stored, and passed to a vector field through a problem's parameters , none of which the old module injection allowed. The ~450 scalar functions are ~41 generics returning tensors, each taking the field first. B¹(t, q) becomes B♯(field, t, q)[1] and dAᵢdxⱼ(t, q) becomes DA♭(field, t, q)[i, j] . The names use the musical isomorphisms — ♭ covariant, ♯ contravariant, ♮ physical, the bare letter the magnitude — and Changed below has the full old-to-new table. Every one of the ~444 old scalar values is an entry of one of the new tensors. The per-field submodules are flattened into the package. Solovev.ITER() is SolovevEquilibriumITER() , ThetaPinch.init() is ThetaPinchEquilibrium() , and so on for every field; Solovev.ITER(xpoint = true) and its siblings are gone in favour of the named X-point constructors. The coordinate helpers X , Y , Z , R , r , θ , ϕ and r² are package-level generics and deliberately not exported — reach them as ElectromagneticFields.R or through coordinates(field) . periodicity is no longer answered or exported by this package. GeometricBase.periodic(equ) gives one Bool per coordinate instead, and a chart with no method for it raises a MethodError when a field is built from it, deliberately. Code that assembled a (xmin, xmax) tuple from rangemin / rangemax behind a single flag must now build it from periodic and the bounds. periodicity = periodic(field) is silently wrong , not an error: a three-element Bool vector destructures to (false, false) . parameters(field) for a Solov'ev equilibrium now includes the coefficient vector c . A₃ reads it, so it travels with the other parameters instead of being frozen into the code. A field rebuilt after clear_field_cache!() is equal to a few ULP, not bit for bit. Compare two builds of one field with a tolerance rather than == . SymEngine is no longer a dependency ; Symbolics, StaticArrays, GeometricBase and ConstructionBase are. The Julia floor stays 1.10. Added Aqua.jl runs as part of the test suite , in test/aqua_tests.jl , which calls Aqua.test_all . This package carried no package-level quality check of any kind before, so all eight — method ambiguities, unbound type parameters, undefined exports, the agreement between Project.toml and test/Project.toml , stale dependencies, [compat] bounds, type piracy and persistent tasks — start from a clean pass rather than from a list of known failures. Two of them cover something this package does structurally. test_piracies covers the eight methods added to GeometricBase's periodic , functions and parameters , each of which dispatches on a type defined here; a new chart family brings a periodic method with it, so the property outlasts any list of the sites. test_undefined_exports covers an export list dominated by the musical-isomorphism accessors, which are defined across src/analytic/ rather than beside the export. The test suite has a test/Project.toml of its own , carrying Aqua, CairoMakie, LinearAlgebra, SafeTestsets, StaticArrays and Test, each with a [compat] bound. The [extras] and [targets] sections of the package's Project.toml are gone with it, together with the CairoMakie bound that belonged to them. Test dependencies that only [extras] declared carried no bounds at all, which is what Aqua.test_deps_compat reports. Changed The symbolic engine is replaced from SymEngine.jl to Symbolics.jl. Dependencies change: SymEngine is removed, Symbolics, StaticArrays, GeometricBase and ConstructionBase are added. Julia floor stays 1.10. GeometricBase is there for the generic names functions ,

items.summary: Anticoncentration is a key ingredient in complexity theoretic arguments for quantum advantage from Gaussian boson sampling. Here we prove polynomial small ball anticoncentration for complex Gaussian transpose Gram hafnians and complex symmetric Gaussian hafnians. For a k × 2n matrix X with independent standard complex Gaussian entries, we establish polynomial small ball anticoncentration for haf(XᵀX) under k ≥ 4n and n²/k = O(log n). For hafnians of 2n × 2n complex symmetric Gaussian matrices, polynomial small ball anticoncentration holds for every n ≥ 1. In both ensembles, any prescribed inverse polynomial failure probability can be achieved with an inverse polynomial small ball radius, uniformly over all centers. These results go beyond moment based anticoncentration by controlling the probability of small hafnian amplitudes. The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. Files: main.pdf contains the main article (14 pages); supplement.pdf contains the supplementary proofs and additional results (33 pages). Related Lean verification sources: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22554594 and https://github.com/HongruZhao/ComplexGramHafnians.
items.title: Local Anticoncentration for Gaussian Boson Sampling via Conditional Wishart Geometry

items.summary: Code and data to reproduce all analyses and the figure in O'Dea et al. (2026) "Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama's anchoveta fishery and its exports". Includes Python scripts for the reef-logger upwelling indices, the bay-wide composite index, the observer set records, the anchoveta length and weight series, the unified 1956 to 2025 landings series, and the main figure together with every statistic reported in the paper. Data include weekly sonde casts from the three deep central stations of the Bay of Panama, continuous reef temperature loggers from the Gulf of Panama running since 1995, the Copernicus Marine Service biogeochemical reanalysis of net primary production (1994 to 2026), anchoveta and thread herring landings spliced from the digitised national stock assessment (1956 to 2014) and the ARAP landings register (2015 to 2025, 332,610 records across 206 taxa), 3,077 onboard observer purse-seine set records (2017 to 2025), 645 dockside proximate assays of landed anchoveta (2016 to 2025), and fish oil and fishmeal export tabulations from INEC customs statistics (1997 to 2025). The archive is self-contained and rebuilds the figure and all reported statistics from the raw sources whenever the derived and figures directories are deleted. Instructions for use, including execution order, software dependencies, directory structure, the provenance of every source and the known caveats, are in README.md. Data are released under CC BY 4.0 and code under the MIT Licence.
items.title: Code and data for: Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama's anchoveta fishery and its exports

items.summary: Embarrassingly parallel workloads, such as parameter sweeps, Monte Carlo simulations, and hyperparameter searches, are pervasive in research computing, yet running a single experiment across a mix of laptops, lab servers, cloud virtual machines (VMs), and high-performance computing (HPC) clusters still demands ad hoc Secure Shell (SSH) tunnels, port forwarding, and scheduler-specific scripts. We present DART, a job distributor that turns any such mix of machines into a single shared queue. DART pairs a Dockerized job server with a one-line worker command-line interface (CLI); a hosted Hub automates reverse tunneling, worker authentication, and public endpoint provisioning, so collaborators on any network, including those behind network address translation (NAT) or using a personal laptop, can join an experiment with a single API-key and no firewall changes. This makes DART especially effective for researchers who combine Advanced Cyberinfrastructure Coordination Ecosystem: Services & Support (ACCESS)-provisioned HPC resources [1] with institutional clusters and personal workstations, federating all resources under one queue with no per-site configuration. All communication is encrypted end-to-end, and access is controlled through API-key authentication and a personal identification number (PIN)-protected dashboard. Researchers create experiments, define parameter grids, and monitor jobs entirely from a web dashboard; a work-conserving scheduler dispatches jobs on demand, exploits resource heterogeneity, and automatically re-queues failures. In a real-world deployment of 37,720 jobs across 68 heterogeneous machines spanning an institutional HPC cluster, a national ACCESS resource, and personal computers, the observed run completed in approximately eight days. DART’s dynamic allocation achieved a simulation-derived 35× speedup over static partitioning (≈4 days vs. ≈139 days), reducing a multi-month workload to days.
items.title: DART: Distributed Assignment of Research Tasks for Heterogeneous Compute Environments

items.summary: README – Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics (CGMD) Simulations of PIEZO1 and TRPM4 Overview This dataset contains coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 and the non-mechanoprotective ion channel TRPM4 embedded in lipid bilayers. The simulations comprise 500 ns of equilibrium followed by membrane stretching simulations designed to investigate how PIEZO1's distinctive triskelion blade architecture redistributes mechanical stress and preserves membrane integrity. All simulations were performed using GROMACS with the Martini 3 force field. Independent replicate simulations (n = 3) were conducted for each system to ensure statistical robustness and reproducibility. Simulation Details Parameter Description Molecular dynamics engine : GROMACS v2021.2 Force field : Martini 3 Membrane model : Lipid bilayer containing either PIEZO1 or TRPM4 Equilibration : 500 ns Stretching simulations : Three independent replicates (n = 3); 50 ns Simulation temperature, pressure, and all additional parameters are provided in the accompanying simulation input files (.mdp) and described in the associated publication. Biological Significance PIEZO1 is a mechanosensitive ion channel whose unique triskelion blade architecture protects cellular membranes from mechanical failure. Its extended peripheral blades redistribute mechanical stress across the lipid bilayer, reducing localized stress accumulation and delaying membrane rupture during mechanical loading. This dataset enables quantitative investigation of how membrane protein architecture influences membrane mechanics, force redistribution, and mechanoprotection using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. Dataset Structure 1. Equilibrium Simulations These simulations characterize the equilibrated membrane environment surrounding each ion channel before mechanical loading. Simulation length: 500 ns PIEZO1_equilibrium.pdb PIEZO1_equilibrium.xtc TRPM4_equilibrium.pdb TRPM4_equilibrium.xtc 2. Membrane Stretching Simulations Following equilibration, membrane stretch was induced using semi-isotropic pressure coupling, with −5 bar applied in the membrane plane (x–y) while maintaining +1 bar normal to the bilayer (z-axis) using the Parrinello–Rahman barostat. PIEZO1 PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.edr PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.edr PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.edr TRPM4 TRPM4_Stretch_R1.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R1.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R1.edr TRPM4_Stretch_R2.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R2.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R2.edr TRPM4_Stretch_R3.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R3.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R3.edr Data Usage The trajectory (.xtc) and coordinate (.pdb) files can be analysed using standard molecular dynamics software, including GROMACS, VMD, and PyMOL. The (.edr) files are also provided for energy calculations and to be utilized -b 0 -e 50000 (time 0 - 50 ns) These simulations support quantitative analyses described in the associated publication. PIEZO1 safeguards membranes under mechanical stress via permeation-independent structural adaptation and calcium-dependent cytoskeletal reinforcement. Cell Press Blue. (2026). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpblue.2026.100128
items.title: PIEZO1 safeguards membranes under mechanical stress using MD simulation

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
items.title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

items.summary: This paper asks a narrow question. Lyapunov stability, geometric stability, and statistical stability are all described as spectral-gap properties. The gaps act on different operators, live on different spaces, and survive different perturbations. The informal habit of treating them as one nested hierarchy is correct for convex wells and hyperbolic sinks. It is not correct as a statement about dynamical systems in general. The paper replaces that habit with a comparison theorem. A stability claim is a profile: an evolution, a perturbation class, a projection, and a failure set. Comparative type can change when the map is held fixed and only the projection changes. Three statistical properties are kept distinct. The first is weak continuity of an invariant measure under perturbation. The second is a spectral gap of a transfer or Fokker–Planck operator on a named function space. The third is differentiability of the measure in the perturbation parameter. These three can hold together. They can also separate. The proved implications are scoped. A positive Hessian implies Lyapunov stability of a mechanical equilibrium and a dissipative Jacobian gap for a gradient flow. A hyperbolic sink gives weak continuity of a Dirac family and does not give mixing on a positive-dimensional density space. Uniform hyperbolicity gives a transfer-operator gap on an anisotropic space and, in the perturbation class of Keller and Liverani, weak continuity of an SRB family. Partial hyperbolicity yields a gap only after restriction to the hyperbolic factor. Nonuniform hyperbolicity with a Young tower yields a slower, tail-controlled rate and is compatible with instability of almost every orbit. A prescribed decay for a piecewise expanding map or a hypocoercive generator need not come from any hyperbolic splitting. Architectural estimates do not transfer between structurally distinct operator classes. In one linear-quadratic noise model the three classical tests return the same number. In a double well they separate. The paper does not claim that statistical mechanisms are finite, and it does not prove that averaging a frequency-gap Hamiltonian system produces a kinetic spectral gap.
items.title: Which Spectral Gaps Imply Which: Lyapunov, Geometric, and Statistical Criteria

items.summary: Abstract The stability of the banking sector is fundamental to economic growth and financial system resilience, particularly in developing economies such as Nigeria.  However, and sadly enough, global, recent and recurring failure risks and collapses of banks which have been blamed on poor external audit qualities, are counter-productive to national economic development.  Therefore, the broad objective of this study was to study the effect of audit quality on failure risks of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria between the period 2009 and 2024. This study adopted both descriptive and ex-post facto research designs.  Using secondary data extracted from audited financial reports of 11 censored (from a population of 11) deposit money banks listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group, (NGX), and analyzing one hundred and seventy-six firm year observations using regression with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors analysis technique, the findings revealed that audit firm size (AUFS) significantly improve bank Z score, [coef. = 0.638 (p-value = 0.005)], audit report timeliness (ARTIME) significantly reduces bank Z score [coef. = −0.400 (p-value = audit committee diligence (ACDI) revealed a positive insignificant effect respectively on Z score of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria during the period under consideration. Based on the above findings, it was concluded that audit quality in the Nigerian banking sector is not uniformly effective, rather, its effect on bank failure risks is selective, with only specific audit mechanisms demonstrating the capacity to significantly enhance financial solvency, thereby suggesting that the effectiveness of external audit as a safeguard against bank failure risks depend not merely on its presence, but likely on factors such as depth, credibility, and functional execution of its key components.   this study concluded that audit.  Consequently, this study recommended among others, that listed deposit money banks in Nigeria, alongside regulators and external auditors, should prioritize substantive governance quality, auditor competence and independence, rigorous audit execution, timely financial reporting, risk-sensitive audit remuneration, coordinated assurance mechanisms, and proactive internal control systems over mere procedural compliance, in order to strengthen transparency, reinforce market confidence, and enhance long term financial stability in line with Agency theory. Keywords: Audit Quality, Failure Risks of Listed Deposit Money Banks, Bank Z-Score, Agency Theory.
tags: Audit Quality, Failure Risks of Listed Deposit Money Banks, Bank Z-Score, Agency Theory.
items.title: Audit Quality and Failure Risks of Listed Deposit Money Banks In Nigeria

Three literal question-mark pairs in plain-text extraction were confined to the arrow glyphs of one Xy-pic diagram on physical page 192. The already generated full-resolution render shows the intended arrows correctly; the finding is a ToUnicode limitation of an inherited diagram font, not missing visible content. Editable TeX and rendered formulae and diagrams remain authoritative where legacy mathematics-font extraction is lossy. The stable Korean EGA concept DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.21921513 ; this exact version is 10.5281/zenodo.22864049 . The public source, issue history, and releases are maintained at github.com/KokunoYumeto/ega-ko . This is the existing Korean EGA lineage, not a competing record and not a merger with FGA, SGA, Chinese, or Japanese editions. items.summary: We present an HTTP threat detection system embedded in a production reverse proxy that achieves sub-500ns per-request inference latency. The system combines a depth-limited CART decision tree with a compact two-layer MLP in an ensemble architecture, where the tree provides fast-path classification and the MLP refines uncertain cases. Model weights are exported as Rust `const` arrays, enabling zero-allocation deployment with no runtime deserialization. We formalize structural safety properties of the ensemble in the Lean~4 theorem prover, establishing a three-tier verification approach covering structural invariants, weight-dependent decision bounds, and floating-point error propagation. In initial small-scale trials on a combined dataset of production logs, CSIC-2010, and CIC-IDS2017-derived features, the ensemble achieves >99% validation accuracy for both scanner and DDoS detection, with tree inference completing in under 2ns and full ensemble inference under 6ns. We discuss limitations of the current training data and outline directions for scaling to larger, human-labeled corpora.
items.title: Sub-Microsecond HTTP Threat Detection with Decision Tree–MLP Ensembles and Lean 4 Verification

items.summary: This dataset contains analysis-ready spatial data on informal urban conditions, heat and flood exposure, slum population, and malaria burden across sub-Saharan Africa.   The deposit includes a processed subnational dataset with 4,320 administrative units, a 44-feature country/region boundary layer, annual HI406 and WBGT30 heat-exposure rasters for 2011–2020, a slum-population raster, a complete data dictionary, descriptive statistics, raster metadata, provenance documentation, rights guidance, and integrity checksums.   The vector data are provided as ESRI Shapefiles and the gridded data as GeoTIFF files. All spatial datasets use WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). The raster grids contain 1,141 columns by 1,235 rows at approximately 0.060362 degrees per cell.   The malaria indicators are population-weighted estimates mapped from source administrative-unit means onto the common slum-population grid. The original upstream flood and malaria source layers are not redistributed in this record. Users should consult the included README, data dictionary, provenance documentation, sources and limitations, and data-use notes before reuse.   This record contains data and data documentation only. Code, notebooks, manuscripts, figures, and supplementary documents are maintained separately in the project repository: https://github.com/JinRuii/informal-urban-climate-malaria-ssa
items.title: Analysis-ready spatial data on informal urban conditions, climate exposure and malaria burden across sub-Saharan Africa

items.summary: This dataset is the frozen, reproducible evidence package supporting the manuscript Value Flow Mechanics for Mining Optimization through the LUJO Protocol. It links the version 1.1 manuscript, claim ledger, limitations, figures, tables, provenance records, and cryptographic manifests. The package contains five closed evidence blocks: the synthetic MFV-MB-01 finite-space benchmark, the historical BM-LUJO integrity reconstruction, the Zuck Large comparator and falsification record, the author-generated Marvin/Whittle pit-curve analysis through MVSC, and the KD scheduling evidence with a declared local exact window. Portable scripts support read-only claim auditing and declared reconstruction paths. Author-created manuscript/results are released under CC BY 4.0; author-created code is released under the MIT License; included MineLib materials retain CC BY-SA 3.0. GEOVIA Whittle, the underlying Marvin model, and excluded project/model files are not redistributed. GEOVIA Whittle, the underlying Marvin model, and excluded project/model files are not redistributed. The evidence is mathematical, computational, synthetic, documentary, and public-benchmark based. It does not constitute comprehensive industrial validation, does not establish universal superiority over existing optimizers, and must be interpreted under the limitations supplied with the package.
items.title: Value Flow Mechanics for Mining Optimization through the LUJO Protocol: Reproducible Evidence Package

items.summary: Administrative disability registries record certified cases, not disability as such: a person absent from the registry may lack certification because no certifiable impairment exists, because access to an evaluation board was unavailable, or because an evaluation is pending - three epistemically distinct situations that a single observed count cannot, by itself, distinguish. This paper reframes a nationwide descriptive analysis of Ecuador's National Disability Registry (Registro Nacional de Discapacidades, CONADIS/MSP; cut-off December 2023; N = 113,203 aggregated records representing 480,776 certified persons across 222 province-canton units) as an instance of typed abstention applied to administrative subregistration. We distinguish "not registered" (no consta: absence of a positive record, uninformative about the underlying condition) from a hypothetical "registered negative" (consta que no: an explicit denial after evaluation, a state that exists within the underlying certification process but is not exposed in the published open-data resource used here) and from internally conflicting evidence. Data quality auditing verified 100% structural completeness across all eight operational fields. The demographic and clinical profile shows a predominance of males (56.48%), adults aged 51 years and older (47.13%), physical disabilities (44.87%), and moderate impairment severity (45.78%). Guayaquil and Quito concentrate 30.83% of absolute registration volume, yet fall to the 134th and 144th of 221 population-normalized ranks, below the national median. Because the published registry cannot, by construction, separate certification capacity from underlying need, we add an illustrative synthetic simulation in which two data-generating mechanisms - pure certification-capacity heterogeneity and pure prevalence heterogeneity, each confounded with population size - produce observable correlations between the normalized rate and population that differ by only 0.021 (Pearson r = 0.949 vs. 0.928) despite sharing no causal mechanism, formalizing why the normalized rate cannot be read as need without an explicit, currently unavailable, capacity signal. We situate this identification problem within the literature on disability statistics (the Washington Group on Disability Statistics; the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health), administrative and missing-data quality, and evidential reasoning frameworks for typed indeterminacy (Dempster-Shafer belief functions, three- and four-valued logics, AGM belief revision), none of which have previously been applied to a cantonal-level disability registry of this kind.
items.title: Typed Abstention in Administrative Disability Registries: Certification Intensity, Subregistration, and the Limits of Cantonal Normalization in Ecuador's National Disability Registry (2023)

items.summary: Industry 4.0 transforms manufacturing through cyber-physical systems, the Industrial Internet of Things, digital twins, and data-driven intelligence, yet the volume of latency-sensitive data these technologies generate strains conventional cloud-only computing. Edge and fog computing have emerged as the central enabling paradigm, distributing computation across a device–fog–cloud continuum. This paper surveys the enabling technologies of Industry 4.0 with an emphasis on edge–cloud computing and formulates the resulting computation-offloading problem as a constrained, load-dependent optimization model that jointly minimizes task latency and device energy under deadline and capacity constraints. A genetic algorithm and a particle swarm optimizer are developed and benchmarked against five baseline strategies on synthetic industrial workloads. Across one hundred tasks averaged over ten instances, the genetic algorithm reduced the weighted objective by 34.1 percent relative to a greedy heuristic and by 82.6 percent relative to cloud-only execution, while lowering deadline violations to 1.6 percent. The latency–energy trade-off, convergence, and scalability are analyzed, and managerial implications for industrial deployment are discussed.
items.title: Energy- and Latency-Aware Computation Offloading in Edge–Fog–Cloud Architectures for Industry 4.0

items.summary: Recent agentic campaigns show that coordinated AI systems can compress reconnaissance, exploitation, and credential harvesting into machine-tempo operations. This paper asks a narrow question: whether increasing the number of untrusted attack sources changes the authorization outcome of an inline control that mediates every protected path and permits only explicit device-to-device relations. Under stated assumptions of complete mediation, fixed and correct policy, uncompromised trust anchors, no alternate path, and sufficient enforcement capacity, it does not. Additional untrusted source identities create additional denied first-contact events, not a permitted relation. This is a conditional property of the authorization rule, not a claim that throughput, alert volume, or availability are independent of swarm size. A four-run laboratory test of an AutoGen agent using GPT-4o provides a mechanism demonstration: the agent created four fresh network identities, and each was denied at its first observed unauthorized probe. The test does not establish a population rate or current-frontier performance. A closed-form illustration shows why reconnaissance opportunity grows with total probe volume when no relation enforcement exists, while the authorization outcome remains denial under the stated assumptions. Residual risks include fingerprinting, compromise of a trusted endpoint, policy error, incomplete path coverage, implementation bypass, and resource exhaustion. Detection remains necessary for evidence and follow-on response; the narrower claim is that alert-only detection should not be the primary containment mechanism for a machine-tempo campaign.
items.title: The AI Agent Swarm Meets First Contact: Conditions Under Which Preventive Relation Enforcement Is Scale-Invariant

items.summary: QSMART — the authors' ORIGINAL MATLAB toolbox (v1.0), run as the full pipeline: Laplacian phase unwrapping, magnitude-weighted echo fitting (with its native R_0 reliability mask), Frangi-filter vasculature masking (with N4 bias correction), two-stage spatially-dependent filtering (SDF) background removal, two-stage STI-Suite QSM_iLSQR inversion, and dipole-model offset adjustment. Compiled from MATLAB and run on the license-free MATLAB Runtime (+ ANTs N4 in the image). QSM-CI reconstruction method qsmart-matlab . Browse and run it at https://qsmxt.github.io/QSM-CI/submission.html?method=qsmart-matlab .
items.title: QSM-CI method: QSMART (MATLAB) (v2)

items.summary: MATLAB implementation, per-item numeric results and figure code for the study "Dissociating Prompt Quality from Response Compliance in Automated Prompt-Engineering Assessment". A four-agent evaluator running on a locally hosted Qwen 2.5-7B-Instruct judge scores each prompt as an artifact before any response exists, then scores the resulting response twice on identical items: once against criteria extracted from that prompt, and once against a fixed rubric that never sees it. Verifiable constraints are checked with the IFEval reference implementation rather than model-generated labels. The whole pipeline runs on consumer CPU hardware with no external API calls. Contents: src/ the MATLAB agents and run scripts; scripts/ the IFEval verifier and the figure code; data/ a SHA-256 manifest of all 4,275 benchmark prompts and the filtered IFEval subset; results/ per-item results for the main run (n = 500) and the ablation (n = 120), the construct-validation output and the IFEval verification output. Corpus not redistributed. No prompt or response text from LMSYS-Chat-1M or WildChat-1M is included; the LMSYS agreement prohibits transfer to third parties and WildChat-1M carries flow-down obligations under the AI2 ImpACT licence. Prompts appear only as SHA-256 hashes, so an independently rebuilt corpus can be verified as identical to the one used here. The IFEval subset is included in full under Apache-2.0.
items.title: Dissociating Prompt Quality from Response Compliance in Automated Prompt-Engineering Assessment: evaluator, results and figure code

items.summary: Reproducibility archive for a fully computational study of a coupled interface-mode multilayer sensing refractive index and temperature over a 100 K range, accompanying the article "Bias-Aware Detection Limits, Calibration Transfer and Matched-Control Robustness Assessment in Dual-Parameter Photonic Refractive-Index and Temperature Sensing: A Coupled Interface-Mode Multilayer Case Study" by Agah Oktay Ertay and Muhammed Mustafa Ertay, accepted by Sensors (MDPI) on 18 September 2026. Version 1.2.1 is the publication release. It carries version 1.2.0, which the Data Availability Statement of the article names, without changing any number, table, input, model, or analysis script (560 of 572 files byte for byte; the 12 replaced root documents are kept under provenance/v1.2.0/). It adds the figure artwork as published: every graphic of the article and of its Supplementary Material as supplied to the journal (figures/published/), the source that draws the 20 graphics redrawn at the proof stage for typographic reasons (true minus signs, notation, legend placement; code/publication_figures/, with a complete diff against the production source), and a launcher mode that re-renders them from the archived tables. It contains the MATLAB production forward model and driver scripts, the frozen material, geometry and acceptance-criterion input files, and the sensitivity matrix, nonlinear calibration, covariance and probability-of-detection routines, the per-realization Monte Carlo yield and matched-control output tables, the design-search evaluation log, the FDFD, CST, MEEP, MPB and FEniCSx verification models with their exported spectra and convergence histories, and the numerical series behind every figure and table in the article and in its Supplementary Material. Version 1.2.0 adds the analyses of the major revision as a separately runnable stage that uses the archived production routines and the frozen tables of version 1.1.0: the sensitivity of the detection limits to instrument noise and drift, reduced per-device calibration protocols, the complete metric set of the nanolaminate-free stack, an oblique-incidence test of the hyperbolicity condition, and the jointly matched trivial control with its paired benchmark. The 483 source, input, result, figure, and solver files of version 1.1.0 are carried byte for byte; only the root metadata files and the launcher were updated, and the v1.1.0 metadata and checksum manifest are kept under provenance/v1.1.0/. A single launcher runs the integrity check, the full reproduction, the revision stage, or both; a SHA-256 manifest covers every other file in the archive. Code is released under the MIT License (LICENSE-CODE); data, result tables, and figures under CC-BY-4.0 (LICENSE-DATA). The three measured ITO n,k tables are third-party public-domain data (CC0 1.0, via refractiveindex.info, originating from Minenkov et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 16, 9517-9531, 2024) and should be cited from that source. The study is numerical. No multilayer was fabricated and no spectrum measured; agreement between independent solvers is not offered as experimental validation.
items.title: Bias-Aware_Detection_Limits_Calibration_Transfer_and_Matched-Control_Robustness_Assessment_in_Dual-Parameter_Photonic_Refractive-Index_and_Temperature_Sensing_A_Coupled_Interface-Mode_Multilayer_Case_Study_All_Software_Package_and_Data_v1.2.1

items.summary: A three-signal stopping rule for iterative LLM refinement derived from the Möbius theory stack: an equilibrium-distance surrogate d̂_R (RZGM meaning-equilibrium layer), an update-free-recurrence and diversity-collapse detector pair (Reflective Homeostasis Layer), and a hard reflection-depth cap (MUSE bounded reflection). Pre-registered study: 500 English prose-refinement tasks across ten domains, two generator models (Gemma4 12B-IT-QAT and 26B-A4B-IT-QAT), 8,000 generations, 999 blind position-swapped pairwise judgments. The governor cuts refinement tokens by 36.6% / 33.1% (bootstrap 95% CIs 33.6-39.5% / 30.3-35.9%) versus an always-eight-iterations baseline — 2.2-3.4x a naive convergence stop — at a measured quality cost reported at equal prominence: 38.0% / 36.6% of judged comparisons lost overall, a majority among actual interventions (61.1% / 59.0%), with measured cost almost perfectly collinear with output length. A full-data ablation shows the saturation signal is simultaneously the savings engine and the dominant cost source, yielding a measured two-point dial (10.0-11.5% savings at 8.2-11.8% loss rate with saturation disabled). Pre-release adversarial verification (four independent refuter passes) confirmed all headline statistics against the raw data and caught an inverted flagship anecdote: the corpus's two catastrophic degenerations (~50 verbatim paragraph repetitions) were selected once and avoided once by the governor, undetected in both cases — set-based trigram signals are structurally blind to within-output verbatim repetition. All tasks, rollouts, verdicts, audit votes, and analysis code are released in the companion repository. AI co-observer: Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic) — working method only; blind pairwise judging by Claude subagents under a position-swapped two-vote protocol; four independent adversarial refuter passes preceded release; the registered author is the human author alone. Version 1.1 (2026-09-19): adds (i) a proof-backed clarification that at window 3 the saturation condition is exactly “three identical consecutive non-rewrite change types” (the 0.70 threshold is inert there; companion note DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22842506), (ii) a pre-registered evaluation of a repetition-ratio guard as a fourth, roll-back signal — fires on both known collapses and 200/200 synthetic inflations, on 0 of 7,998 remaining published generations, 0 of 60 template expansions, and 0 of 960 held-out generations (verdict GO; pre-registration commit a89f722 precedes all evaluation data), and (iii) an expanded AI-authorship disclosure. All v1.0 numbers are unchanged. Version 1.2 (2026-09-19): adds (i) a length-stratified reanalysis of the 621 judged governor pairs (loss rate 92% where the early text is under 60% of the final length, 16.1% at near-equal length; 31 losses vs 4 wins at matched length, sign test p < 10 -5 — evidence of a content cost independent of length, not a decomposition of the headline cost), (ii) a held-out replication on 60 tasks authored after the fourth-signal pre-registration (token reduction 34.5% / 34.5%, loss rate 31.7% / 36.7%, main-study values inside the held-out intervals), and (iii) an online-intervention verification: an incremental governor reproduces all 1,000 published decisions (0 mismatches) and, run as a genuine online loop on the 60 held-out tasks with the 12B generator, generates 319 of 480 iterations with a stop distribution indistinguishable from the offline policy (permutation p = 0.46). All v1.0 and v1.1 numbers are unchanged. Version 1.3 (2026-09-19): adds a pre-registered length-matched re-judging (100 governor-loss pairs with early/final length ratio < 0.80; final text truncated at sentence boundaries to the early text's word count): the early text beats the length-matched final in 94/100 (loss 4%), and the full final beats its own truncation in 100/100. Pre-registered label: the losses on this stratum are attributab
items.title: The Reflective Budget Governor: Equilibrium-Based Early Stopping for Iterative LLM Refinement

items.summary: Self-contained synthetic seismic–gravity inversion models, Python operators, seeds, archived and profile-initialized fits, regional controls, posterior samples, figures and validation records for the manuscript by Emilson P. Leite and Maiara M. Gonçalves. Version 0.11 adds a four-start calibration on 96 paired noise comparisons, an audit of unchanged displayed seismic median errors, exact n=32 coverage intervals, and empirical bias–variance accounting of the existing regional controls. The four-start shortcut did not reproduce the profile solutions; the manuscript retains 32 profile-initialized noise pairs for each free-geometry configuration. Fixed-geometry ensembles retain 256 realizations. Wide local intervals under a free trend coexist with systematic target-property errors directed towards the prior. No new posterior chains were generated in this revision. Field observations and third-party BP-model data are not required.
items.title: When gravity adds useful information to interpretation-conditioned post-stack seismic inversion: reproducibility archive
